newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TNVZ chief executive to resign after two years.
newsitem.headline: TNVZ chief executive to resign after two years.

text.p: The chief executive of national television company TVNZ, Chris Anderson, is to resign, the company announced on Wednesday.
TVNZ said in a statement that Anderson had received a job approach from abroad and wanted to be free to accept it.
Chariman Rosanne Meo said an international search would start immediately to find a successor as Anderson was due to leave in early September.
The Australian's resignation, after two years with TVNZ, came in a week when a senior management shakeup at the company has been made public.

Earlier this week the company announced that director of corporate planning and development Bruce Wallace would leave next month and that Doug Northey, general manager of human resources and information technology, was to quit.
TVNZ's executive committee has been cut by three to six people in the last week.
Meo said in the statement that Anderson had put in place a strong executive team "which he consolidated with this week's announcement".
She added he had made a major contribution to the company's restructuring and brand repositioning over the past two years.
